name: Old Town (Stariat Grad) around Samovodska Charshia
tagline: Historic craft street and postcard river views
description: The atmospheric heart of Veliko Tarnovo, where cobbled lanes and old houses stack up the slopes around the historic Samovodska Charshia craft street. Cafes, workshops and mehanas cluster here, with the Tsarevets fortress and gorge views a short walk away.
bestFor: History lovers and short-stay nomads wanting atmosphere and walkable charm
pros: Rich medieval character and craft shops

name: Varusha quarter
tagline: Revival-era streets on the quiet slopes
description: A characterful old residential quarter of nineteenth-century Revival houses climbing the hillside just above the Old Town. Varusha is quieter and more local, with churches, restored facades and steep lanes, yet still within easy walking distance of the centre and its cafes.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads wanting character, calm and a local residential feel
pros: Close to the Old Town on foot
cons: Very hilly and demanding to walk

name: Modern centre (Mother Bulgaria square and Nezavisimost)
tagline: Everyday hub with cafes and shops
description: The practical, contemporary heart of town around Mother Bulgaria square and Nezavisimost street. This is where you find banks, supermarkets, study-friendly cafes and reliable wifi, along with a steady flow of students and locals going about daily life.
bestFor: Remote workers wanting cafes, amenities and easy day-to-day convenience
pros: Best selection of cafes and wifi
All everyday shops and services close by
cons: Less historic charm than the Old Town

name: Kartala / university area
tagline: Student district with the best value
description: The lively student side of Veliko Tarnovo around the university, including the Kartala area. Cheaper flats, casual eateries and a young, sociable energy define it, making it popular with those chasing value and a relaxed, buzzing everyday atmosphere.
bestFor: Budget nomads and sociable long-stayers wanting cheap rent and student energy
